wa_wildcat_wall.blurb: Wildcat Wall is the main attraction of the Wildcat Creek area in the Tieton River region of south-central Washington. Tall basalt columns, roughly 100 feet high, carry sustained lines that are mostly cracks protected with gear, plus a few bolted routes. The 18 climbs run from 5.8 to 5.12, but most sit at 5.10 and 5.11, so it suits climbers who are comfortable on steady, stout cracks rather than beginners. The wall faces mostly north and stays out of the sun until late afternoon in late spring, which can stretch the Tieton season into warmer months. Few people visit, so it tends to be quiet.
wa_wildcat_wall.parking_note: Leave the car at the barrier across Wildcat Road, roughly 1.7 miles up from Highway 12.
wa_wildcat_wall.approach: Walk or bike about a mile along the old road, crossing two stream gaps where the road has washed out. Pick up the trail that drops on the left, across from Honeycomb Buttress; the wall is a couple of minutes further. There is little elevation gain.

wa_a_wall.blurb: A-Wall is a sport crag in the Fun Rock group of crags near Mazama in the Methow Valley. Its 18 bolted routes run from about 5.7 to 5.12, with the largest cluster at 5.10 and a fair number of 5.11 and 5.12 lines, so intermediates have plenty to choose from and a few lines go beyond that. A couple of routes are long enough that a 60 m rope is advised. Rest and belay spots are shaded while most of the climbing itself is in the sun. A trail leads up to it from the main Fun Rock area, passing Sunbug Slab on the way.

wa_powerhouse_wall.blurb: Powerhouse Wall is a steep basalt cliff in the Powerhouse area of Echo Basin at Frenchman Coulee, near Vantage. It is the tallest, most steadily overhanging layer in the basin, so the climbing is pumpy and favors power-endurance. Of the 18 routes, 16 are bolted and two are trad. About half are 5.11, with a handful of 5.10s, a couple of 5.12s and very few easier lines, and the grades feel stiff for the Coulee. The wall catches sun for most of the day, so an early start helps when it is warm.

wa_hen_house.blurb: Hen House is a basalt wall in the Sunshine's Lower Cliffs section of Echo Basin at Frenchman Coulee, near Vantage. The rock is darker than the neighboring Millennium Wall and is undercut, so many routes open with a tougher move just off the ground. Of the 18 routes, 16 are sport and two are trad. A few easier climbs exist, but most sit at 5.10 and 5.11, with a couple at 5.12. Climbers say the style is closer to the Jigsaw Wall than to the Corn and Millennium walls beside it. It starts just right of the last Millennium route.

wa_lower_rhythm.blurb: Lower Rhythm is the lower wall of the Rhythm Cliff at Index, in the Skykomish Valley. It is a long line of short climbs on tacky rock, mostly trad with a few sport lines and a single top-rope. The 18 routes range from 5.7 to 5.12, with 5.10 the most common grade, a good number of 5.11s and a few easier lines for warming up. You get tested across several different styles rather than one. The wall is freshly scrubbed and easy to spot from the trail, and the short approach makes it a quick stop.
wa_lower_rhythm.approach: From the Upper Town Wall trail, take the left fork toward the Blues, Rhythm and Mid walls. Roughly five minutes along, a signed turn-off on the right leads to the wall, just before the turn for Blues Cliff.

wa_kenticle_boulder.blurb: Kenticle Boulder is a small bouldering wall in Kent, Washington, beside the much taller artificial climbing wall at the Kent East Hill Skate Park. It stands around ten feet high and is slightly overhanging. The 18 problems are mostly easy, running from VB to V3 with the bulk between V0 and V2, and some problems stick to the wall's own features. It is a handy city spot for beginners and for a quick warm-up session near the Seattle area.
